newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest dealers take protection on soybeans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest dealers take protection on soybeans.

text.p: Several U.S. Midwest cash grain dealers reported scattered eight cents a bushel cash protection on old and new crop soybeans in anticipation of a lower CBOT opening.
"We are taking eight cents protection on all old and new soybeans," one Indiana dealer said.
CBOT soybeans were called to open two to four cents per bushel lower on active soybean seedings in the Midwest and weather outlooks conducive for crop development, traders said.
Some dealers said they were following Project A overnight values rather than posting protection. Soybeans were down five to eight cents on Project A.
"Whenever there's a big move in Project A, we usually just go with that," an Iowa dealer said.
